verdict.rationale: Rippling documents headless programmatic access for 'customer or internal automation'. This uses Bearer API tokens against a versioned v2 REST API, with scoped permissions, cursor pagination and an official npm SDK, so non-interactive scripted runs are plausible. There is no CI-specific guidance, no CLI, and no evidence of which IT-module operations (devices, identity, inventory) are exposed through the API. missing for 10: CI/pipeline-specific docs or examples, a headless CLI, documented IT-specific API coverage, independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Customer or internal automation: API tokens created in Tools → Developer → API Tokens. Pass `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `https://rest.ripplingapis.com`.
Pin a dated API version with the `Rippling-Api-Version` header (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
Access is the intersection of the owner’s permission profile and the token’s scopes.
Run `npm view @rippling/rippling-sdk version` or check https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rippling/rippling-sdk before pinning a version.
